title: Clothing Care & Laundry
subtitle: Five symbols, three sorts, and why blood needs cold water.
objectives: Explain why protein stains need cold water

cards.title: The label is a language
cards.text: Every garment comes with written instructions almost nobody is taught to read. Five shapes cover all of it.

cards.title: Five shapes, one cross
cards.text: Learn the shapes and the cross, and you can read any label.
points: **Tub** — washing. **Triangle** — bleach.
**Square** — drying. **Iron** — ironing.
**Circle** — dry cleaning.
**A cross through any of them** means do not.

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each symbol. The second line is what it means in practice.

question.text: A tub symbol with a hand in it means…
question.explain: Usually wool or a loose knit. A machine will felt it.

cards.title: Three sorts, not one
points: **By colour:** whites, lights, darks.
**By fabric:** heavy denim will abrade a thin shirt.
**By soil level:** very dirty items redeposit onto clean ones.
**Turn dark clothes inside out.** The sun fades the outside.

cards.title: Cold water first, always
cards.text: Hot water on the wrong stain makes it permanent.
points: **Blood, egg, milk, sweat** are protein stains.
**Heat cooks protein** and sets it into the fibre.
**Cold water and soap first.** Then wash normally.
**Blot, do not rub.** Rubbing drives it deeper.

question.text: Why does a blood stain need cold water?
options: Heat cooks the protein and sets it

cards.title: Training kit is the hardest laundry there is
cards.text: Sweat is a protein stain and synthetic fabric holds the bacteria that cause the smell.
points: **Do not leave it in the bag.** Hours in a damp bag is the problem.
**Rinse it the same day** if you cannot wash it.
**Cold wash**, because sweat is protein.
**Air dry.** Heat bakes the smell in permanently.

cards.title: A washing machine is a drum and a pump
cards.text: Knowing what is inside explains both rules about loading it.
points: **Clothes need room to tumble** or nothing moves through them.
**Overloading means a dirty, unrinsed load.**
**Too much detergent** cannot be rinsed out and stiffens fabric.
**Both faults look like a broken machine.** Neither is.

cards.title: The instructions were always there
cards.alt: A sewn-in clothing care label showing tub, triangle, square and iron pictograms
cards.text: Tub, triangle, square, iron. Five shapes and a cross is the whole language.

cards.title: It is a maintenance loop
cards.text: A kit that is clean on the day you need it was dealt with three days earlier.
points: **Wash the day it is used.**
**Dry before storing**, or it will smell.
**Fold and put away**, not on a chair.
**The loop breaks at the chair.** Every time.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Tub, triangle, square, iron, circle — and a cross means do not.
Sort by colour, by fabric and by how dirty things are.
Protein stains get cold water first; heat sets them.
Do not overload, do not overdose detergent, dry before storing.

quiz.explain: A number inside is the maximum temperature.

quiz.text: A triangle on a label refers to…
quiz.explain: Crossed out means no bleach at all.
A circle inside means a tumble dryer.

quiz.text: Dots inside the iron symbol indicate…
A symbol with a cross through it means…
quiz.explain: The cross is the whole instruction.
Along with egg, milk and sweat.
quiz.objective: Explain why protein stains need cold water

quiz.text: Protein stains should be treated with…
quiz.explain: Heat cooks the protein into the fibre.
quiz.objective: Explain why protein stains need cold water

quiz.text: Rubbing a fresh stain is the best first move.
quiz.explain: Blot. Rubbing drives it deeper into the fibre.
quiz.objective: Explain why protein stains need cold water

quiz.text: Why turn dark clothes inside out to dry?
quiz.explain: Especially on a line in full sun.

quiz.text: Overloading a washing machine results in…

quiz.explain: It cannot all be rinsed out.

quiz.text: Why should training kit not be left in a bag?
options: Hours damp and warm is what creates the smell
quiz.explain: Rinse the same day if you cannot wash it.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 8 TLE. Care labels are treated as a written language with five shapes and one negation, which is genuinely all of it and makes the whole system learnable in one card. The protein-stain rule is the week's most useful piece of knowledge and is given with its mechanism — heat cooks protein into the fibre — because the mechanism is what makes someone reach for cold water under pressure. The boxing lens is the most directly applicable thing in the subject for this learner: sweat is a protein stain, synthetic kit holds the bacteria that smell, and leaving it in a bag is the actual cause.
discussion: Ask him to read the label on what he is wearing.
Ask why blood needs cold water.
Ask what happens if a machine is overloaded.
Ask what to do with kit when he gets home.
extension: Have him sort a real wash three ways and explain each pile.
Have him treat one protein stain with cold water and one with hot, and compare.
misconceptions: "Hot water cleans better." It sets protein stains permanently.
"More detergent means cleaner." The residue stiffens fabric.
